claims.text: Approving at altitude makes the far-out cases visible but does not answer the ordinary case inside every envelope and covered by no rule: a late but intact order, a deletion asked by someone on the project, a release with a nearly unrelated failing test.
claims.quote: the case that is inside every envelope and still not covered by any rule.

claims.text: A business will never predict all of those cases and should not try; a decision policy that lists every case becomes a contract nobody reads, so it needs a way to settle the unpredicted ones and learn from them.
claims.quote: A decision policy that tries to list every case becomes a contract nobody reads.

claims.text: English law's shape: statutes set principles, delegated rules stay within their powers, courts decide cases with reasons, higher courts bind lower ones, a differing case is distinguished, and precedent can be corrected.
claims.quote: I am not a lawyer, and what follows is the shape, not the detail.

claims.text: In Pepper v Hart in 1992 a court may, in a narrow set of cases, read what the minister said in Parliament to find what a provision was for.
claims.quote: a court may even read what the minister said in Parliament to find what a provision was for.

claims.text: A delegated rule that goes beyond its power is ultra vires and can be quashed, as the employment tribunal fees order was in 2017; that is the narrow-never-widen rule from the second article.
claims.quote: A rule that goes beyond that power is ultra vires and can be quashed, as the employment tribunal fees order was in 2017.

claims.text: The Open University's introduction: if the precedent is from a more senior court than the one hearing the new case it tends to be binding, and deciding that earlier facts are similar but not similar enough is called distinguishing.
claims.quote: If a court decides that the facts in an earlier case are similar, but not similar enough, then this is called distinguishing.

claims.text: In 1966 the House of Lords declared in a Practice Statement that it could depart from its own previous decisions, and the Supreme Court treats that as applying to itself, so a wrong answer is not locked in forever.
claims.quote: A wrong answer is not locked in forever; it can be overruled, by a court with the authority to do it.

claims.text: England and Wales is used because it is the system the owner knows and where precedent works most like the proposal; Scotland's is a mixed system and many others differ.
claims.quote: Scotland's legal system is different, a mixed one, and so are many others.

claims.text: The mapping: an Act is the envelope at the top, delegated legislation is the lower-altitude policies, a court is a person deciding an escalated case, the judgment is the decision record, binding precedent is the next matching case following it.
claims.quote: The loop in the figure is the whole of it. A case arrives at a branch point.

claims.text: The loop: a rule settles the case, or a recorded precedent with the same material facts does; if neither, or the facts differ in a way that matters, it goes to a person, whose recorded decision becomes a precedent the next matching case follows.
claims.quote: Their decision, with the facts and the reasons, becomes a precedent. The next matching case follows it.

claims.text: Agency is not a yes put delegation at the top of its scale: the cases you keep approving unchanged become rules that run without you, as code under a behaviour policy.
claims.quote: The cases you keep approving unchanged become rules that run without you, as code under a behaviour policy.

claims.text: Case law moves a decision up both scales in four steps: a person decides, precedent decides, the policy decides after the precedent has held across enough cases, and code decides once the rule is compiled into a test, check, limit or gate.
claims.quote: Each step is earned by cases, not assumed in advance.

claims.text: The difference from writing every rule up front is that the rules that reach code are the ones reality kept asking for.
claims.quote: the rules that reach code are the ones reality kept asking for.

claims.text: A decision record good enough to be a precedent needs the facts that mattered, the rule and altitude it was decided under, who decided with what authority, the outcome, and the reasons in a sentence or two.
claims.quote: This is the part that makes it a precedent rather than a statistic.

claims.text: Without such a record a system cannot distinguish a case, because it does not know which facts the earlier decision turned on; in the SGit and Ruflo run every policy decision is computed and none is written down.
claims.quote: every policy decision is computed and none is written down.

claims.text: A decision that leaves no record is a self-report at best; most agent systems keep a log, not a report.
claims.quote: A decision that leaves no record is a self-report at best.

claims.text: A new rule from one case: a figure shipped with an unchecked date, the fix was a new version, and the precedent is that a figure's facts are checked like the body's; one case was enough because the rule is cheap.
claims.quote: The precedent is that a figure's facts are checked like the body's.

claims.text: A case distinguished: the status report counted two commits with no leak scan, both in throwaway repositories built to test git hooks that never published anything; the rule stands and the counter should count only repositories the rule covers.
claims.quote: The case is distinguished, the rule stands, and the counter should count only the repositories the rule covers.

claims.text: Courts are slow on purpose; a precedent for an agent can be set in a minute by one person, which is its strength and its risk.
claims.quote: A precedent for an agent can be set in a minute by one person. That is its strength and its risk.

claims.text: Precedent can carry a bias forward: a wrong decision followed a thousand times is a thousand wrong decisions, so the ability to overrule at the right altitude matters more for agents than for courts.
claims.quote: A wrong decision followed a thousand times is a thousand wrong decisions.

claims.text: Nobody argues the other side: a person approving an agent's case usually hears only the agent; asking a second agent for the case against is a review, not a court.
claims.quote: One answer is to ask a second agent for the case against, which is a review, not a court.

claims.text: Material facts is a judgement: deciding whether a case is distinguished is itself a decision, so a model can propose and, at first, a person should decide.
claims.quote: A model can propose; at first, a person should decide.

claims.text: It is not legal advice or a summary of English law; it borrows the shape of precedent, from introductory sources, for a different purpose.
claims.quote: It borrows the shape of precedent, from introductory sources, for a different purpose.

claims.text: It is a proposal: no agent system the owner knows keeps decision records as precedents in this way, and the loop is untested.
claims.quote: No agent system I know of keeps decision records as precedents in this way; the loop is untested.

claims.text: The two cases are small: they show the loop's shape, not that it works at scale.
claims.quote: They show the loop's shape, not that it works at scale.

claims.text: The session's status report counted two commits with no leak scan before them, both in throwaway repositories that never published anything.
claims.quote: The session's status report counted two commits with no leak scan before them.
